messages:
Maya: Quick design pass on the Private setup wizard preflight. The current 'Connectivity' page is overwhelming for new users. Can we reduce noise and show a clear outcome first (Pass / Action needed)?
Diego: Yes. First thing should be a compact result summary card: big green check or red stop, short reason, and 1-2 action CTAs. No logs up-front.
Sam: Proposed states: All good -> green summary + expand details; Non-blocking issues -> amber summary + inline 'Accept risk' button; Blocking -> red summary + required remediation steps.
Priya: Accessibility: ensure the summary card is focused when results render. Use aria-live=\"assertive\" on the summary and aria-describedby on action buttons. Keyboard users must hit the remediation flow immediately.
Maya: For remediation steps, keep copy prescriptive and short. E.g., instead of \"port issue\" write \"Open TCP port 8080 in your firewall to allow health checks.\" Add a single command they can copy for quick verification.
Diego: For logs, add a collapsed 'Diagnostics' panel. It expands to tool-specific snippets and a short replay button: \"Re-run check from our probe\" so users can see if fixes applied.
Sam: UX detail: show a per-check compact status line with an icon, title, and two buttons: 'Run test' (async) and 'Help'. Default to collapsed help.
Priya: VoiceOver note: when a test finishes, announce \"Connection test for <service> failed\" assertively. Progress updates can be polite. Avoid spamming announcements during long checks.
preflight-bot: scan-complete: 6 checks, 2 warnings, 1 blocking failure. See collapsed details.
Maya: On the blocking item (NAT/router not forwarding), replace vague text with: \"Router not forwarding traffic to the instance. Check port forwarding / NAT rules.\" Offer a tailored KB link for common routers and cloud SGs.
Diego: We should include a tolerant 'Preview changes' flow when we propose config edits (e.g., suggest a CIDR or port). Show a diff-style preview and an explicit 'Apply to template' action, not automatic edits.
Sam: Suggest a small inline code block for engineers: ```bash
# from bastion
nc -vz <instance-ip> 8080
``` Keep it hidden behind 'Show command' to avoid scaring non-devs.
Priya: Color contrast: use text labels alongside color icons. Don't rely on red/green alone. Also add a tooltip explaining severity levels with examples.
Maya: Microcopy: replace generic headings like \"Failed checks\" with action-focused copy: \"Action needed: Port 8080 closed\" or \"Optional: TLS cert expires soon\". More context = less support churn.
Diego: Mobile: collapse details, show only summary + primary action. Tapping expands full diagnostics.
Sam: For operations teams, add a 'Download full report' button producing a small JSON with checks and timestamps they can attach to tickets. Keep the file lightweight.
Priya: Keyboard flow: primary actions should be in source order. If a modal opens for 'Proceed with warnings', trap focus and include an accessible checkbox \"I understand the risks\" before enabling Confirm.
preflight-bot: note: replay endpoints will rate limit after 3 attempts per 5m to avoid probe storms.
Maya: Great. I'll draft a Figma mock with the summary-first layout and suggested strings. Diego, can you prototype the collapsed diagnostics and the diff preview? Sam, can you stub the CLI snippets and the download report formatter? Priya, can you run the a11y checklist against the mock?
Diego: On it. I'll also add a tiny 'why this matters' inline link next to each check that opens the KB in a new tab.
Sam: I'll add the streaming status updates per-check (small spinner + final state). That felt much better in previous designs.
Priya: Remember to include labels for assistive tech: role=\"status\" for progress, aria-live variations per guidance.
Maya: Thanks team. Let's aim to ship the prototype next week and test with one customer. :rocket:
